ideas.title: Agent spend guard
ideas.summary: Fable 5 burns a week of $200-plan quota in a day and developers only find out when they hit the wall — the 'too expensive' thread on HN is people who cannot see where their tokens go. Solo builders and small teams running coding agents all day would pay for a local proxy that meters burn per task, flags runaway loops before they eat the quota, and routes mechanical work to cheaper models. Easybilling just claimed the billing side of usage-based AI products; nobody owns the cost-control side of the agent stack yet.

evidence.note: Tell HN: a $200-plan subscriber burned most of a weekly quota in one day on Fable 5 — acute, unmet cost-visibility pain.
Easybilling launched AI-native billing for usage-based AI products — the payments side is taken, the spend-control side is open.

ideas.title: Bring-your-own-agent code review
ideas.summary: CodeRabbit is throttling annual subscribers to two reviews an hour, and the Ask HN thread shows working engineers shopping for a replacement the same day. Teams already paying for review bots would pay for one that runs on the Claude or Codex subscription they already have instead of a metered SaaS — bring-your-own-agent review with repo-aware checklists. Claude Code v2.1.172 shipping nested sub-agents (5 levels deep) makes the fan-out — one reviewer per file, a synthesizer on top — a weekend build rather than an infra project.

evidence.note: Ask HN: paying CodeRabbit customer hit a 2-reviews-per-hour throttle and is actively looking for alternatives.
Claude Code v2.1.172 lets sub-agents spawn sub-agents up to 5 levels deep — the capability that makes per-file review fan-out trivial.
